summary: This Advent sermon examines Mary's response to the angel Gabriel in Luke 1, arguing that she possessed biblical hope—not wishful thinking, but confident expectation in God's promises despite dire circumstances. The message challenges listeners to see hope as both confident expectation rooted in Christ's resurrection and intentional participation in God's work, just as Mary said yes to bearing the Messiah despite the personal cost.
key_points: Advent calls us to look back to Jesus' first coming with gratitude and forward to his return with anticipation
Mary had confident hope God would send the Messiah despite being a poor young girl under Roman oppression
Biblical hope differs from wishful thinking; it is confident expectation rooted in God's character and promises
Our hope is anchored in the resurrection—the empty tomb proves God keeps his promises
God invites us to participate in his promises, not just believe them, empowered by the Holy Spirit
big_idea: Hope is the confident expectation and intentional participation in God's promises, rooted in the resurrection of Jesus and calling us to say yes to whatever God asks.
title: Advent 2024: HOPE
